summary:
PERSEVERE-NET is an interactive 3D simulation and strategy game set in Jezero Crater (18.38°N, 77.58°E), combining autonomous base building, a drivable 6x6 rover, ISRU resource production, and a full Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) rocket launch sequence.
Players establish power grids using solar panels, batteries, and nuclear cores; extract ice and regolith to sustain life support; collect rare iridium and xenon minerals from distant sectors; and construct and fuel the MAV rocket to launch collected Martian samples into orbit. The project gamifies NASA's Mars 2020 Perseverance and Mars Sample Return (MSR) missions—from surface exploration to orbital rocket ascent—to inspire youth interest in space exploration.
details:
• How It Works: Built on a WebGL-based Three.js engine, allowing players to directly control astronauts or the 6x6 rover using keyboard and mouse controls, manage base infrastructure, and execute the final MAV rocket launch sequence to complete the mission.
  • Technologies Used: Three.js (r128), Tailwind CSS, JavaScript ES6+, and Web Audio API (real-time procedural sound synthesis for rover engines, mining, and rocket ignition).
  • Innovative Aspects: A complete end-to-end Mars mission simulation running entirely in the browser using procedural textures without heavy external model assets, featuring a save/load system, bilingual support (EN/TR), and a cinematic rocket launch finale.
  • AI Use: Claude (Anthropic) was used for coding, debugging and performance optimization of the game, and to help draft the demo slides and project text. Textures and sounds are generated procedurally in code; no AI-generated image or audio files are used. The demo slides carry a visible "Slides made with AI assistance" note. No NASA logos, flags or mission insignia are used.
